title: Rav Nachman of Nehardea
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Mentioned in Chullin 95b: he visited Rav Kahana at Pum Nahara on the eve of Yom Kippur. The supplied notice has Rav Nachman tell him, “Take and eat,” etc. Hyman reports that the Rashba’s Chullin commentary reads Rav Chanan of Nehardea.

notes.text: The consulted Davidson translation makes Rav Kahana invite Rav Nachman to eat; the supplied notice explicitly places ר״נ after “said to him.” The English preserves that source attribution as a question rather than silently harmonizing the roles.

The saved whole Davidson Chullin95b scalar explicitly names Rav Nachman of Nehardea visiting Rav Kahana in Pum Nahara on Yom Kippur eve. The invitation has pronouns without a named speaker; Hyman’s ר״נ speaker assignment remains attributed, alongside the inherited English comparison assigning Kahana. The reported Rashba Rav Chanan variant was not newly verified; an earlier failed fetch is not absence proof. No crow/liver/kidney details absent from this notice are imported.

The consulted scan of Hyman, volume III, printed p. 945, reads א״ל ר״כ, assigning “Take and eat” to Rav Kahana, whereas the supplied transcription retained in this translation reads ר״נ. The earlier notes and the translated speaker assignment concern that supplied reading; they do not establish the printed page’s speaker. The consulted Bavli passage names Nachman as the visitor but gives the invitation with pronouns. The Gerlitz/Oraita-labeled digital Rashba on Chullin 95a explicitly says that Rav Kahana told Rav Chanan to take the meat. This confirms a Chanan reading and Kahana’s role in that commentary, but the cited sentence does not independently supply “of Nehardea.” That affiliation remains Hyman’s report. No identification of Nachman with Chanan is admitted, and the supplied Hebrew has not been changed.
